hindi: दैव पीड़न ये हैं — अग्नि, जल, व्याधि, दुर्भिक्ष और मरक।
english: Affliction from the divine: fire, water, disease, famine and pestilence.
lines_deva: दैव.पीडनं - अग्निर् उदकं व्याधिर् दुर्भिक्षं मरक इति
lines_iast: daiva.pīḍanaṃ - agnir udakaṃ vyādhir durbhikṣaṃ maraka iti

words.gloss: whose harm can be crossed over

hindi: "अग्नि और जल में से अग्नि का पीड़न प्रतिकार-रहित और सब कुछ जला देने वाला है, जबकि जल के पीड़न से बचकर निकला जा सकता है और उसकी बाधा को पार किया जा सकता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of fire and water, affliction by fire is irremediable and burns everything, while affliction by water can be escaped from and its harm can be crossed over,' say the teachers.
lines_deva: "अग्न्य्.उदकयोर् अग्नि.पीडनम् अप्रतिकार्यं सर्व.दाहि च, शक्य.अपगमनं तार्य.आबाधम् उदक.पीडनम्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "agny.udakayor agni.pīḍanam apratikāryaṃ sarva.dāhi ca, śakya.apagamanaṃ tārya.ābādham udaka.pīḍanam" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.

text_flags.why: 'it' is not a word; every parallel line in this chapter reads na-iti (iti). Probable typing slip.

notes: Read as na iti.
lines_deva: न-इत् कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-it kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: अग्नि एक गाँव या आधा गाँव जलाती है, परन्तु जल का वेग सौ गाँवों को बहा ले जाता है।
english: Fire burns a village or half a village, but a flood of water sweeps away a hundred villages.
lines_deva: अग्निर् ग्रामम् अर्ध.ग्रामं वा दहति, उदक.वेगस् तु ग्राम.शत.प्रवाही-इति
lines_iast: agnir grāmam ardha.grāmaṃ vā dahati, udaka.vegas tu grāma.śata.pravāhī-iti

words.gloss: through the stoppage of the activity of the dead, the sick, those stricken and the attendants
words.gram: m. inst. sg. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

hindi: "व्याधि और दुर्भिक्ष में से व्याधि मृतों, रोगियों, पीड़ितों और परिचारकों के व्यायाम के रुक जाने से कर्मों को नष्ट करती है; दुर्भिक्ष तो कर्मों को नष्ट नहीं करता और हिरण्य, पशु तथा कर देने वाला होता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of disease and famine, disease ruins works through the stoppage of the activity of the dead, the sick, those stricken and those attending on them; famine, on the other hand, does not ruin works and yields gold, cattle and taxes,' say the teachers.
notes: upasṛṣṭa taken as 'those stricken (by the disease)'; vyāyāma rendered 'activity' per glossary.
lines_deva: "व्याधि.दुर्भिक्षयोर् व्याधिः प्रेत.व्याधित.उपसृष्ट.परिचारक.व्यायाम.उपरोधेन कर्माण्य् उपहन्ति, दुर्भिक्षं पुनर् अकर्म.उपघाति हिरण्य.पशु.कर.दायि च" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "vyādhi.durbhikṣayor vyādhiḥ preta.vyādhita.upasṛṣṭa.paricāraka.vyāyāma.uparodhena karmāṇy upahanti, durbhikṣaṃ punar akarma.upaghāti hiraṇya.paśu.kara.dāyi ca" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: व्याधि एक ही प्रदेश को पीड़ित करती है और उसका प्रतीकार किया जा सकता है, किन्तु दुर्भिक्ष समस्त देश को पीड़ित करता है और प्राणियों के जीवन का नाश कर देता है।
english: Disease afflicts one region and can be remedied; famine afflicts the whole country and leads to the loss of life of living beings.
lines_deva: एक.देश.पीडनो व्याधिः शक्य.प्रतीकारश् च, सर्व.देश.पीडनं दुर्भिक्षं प्राणिनाम् अजीवनाय-इति
lines_iast: eka.deśa.pīḍano vyādhiḥ śakya.pratīkāraś ca, sarva.deśa.pīḍanaṃ durbhikṣaṃ prāṇinām ajīvanāya-iti

hindi: उसी से मरक की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By that, pestilence is explained.
lines_deva: तेन मरको व्याख्यातः
lines_iast: tena marako vyākhyātaḥ

words.gloss: of the loss of lesser men and the loss of chiefs
having the nature of obstructing the carrying out of works

hindi: "क्षुद्रकों और मुख्यों के क्षय में से क्षुद्रकों का क्षय कर्मों के योग-क्षेम का अभाव करता है, जबकि मुख्यों का क्षय कर्मों के अनुष्ठान में बाधा डालने के स्वभाव वाला है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of the loss of lesser men and the loss of chiefs, the loss of lesser men brings about lack of acquisition and security for works; the loss of chiefs has the nature of obstructing the carrying out of works,' say the teachers.
notes: kṣudraka = lesser men, the rank and file; mukhya = chiefs, leading men.
lines_deva: "क्षुद्रक.मुख्य.क्षययोः क्षुद्रक.क्षयः कर्मणाम् अयोग.क्षेमं करोति, मुख्य.क्षयः कर्म.अनुष्ठान.उपरोध.धर्मा" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "kṣudraka.mukhya.kṣayayoḥ kṣudraka.kṣayaḥ karmaṇām ayoga.kṣemaṃ karoti, mukhya.kṣayaḥ karma.anuṣṭhāna.uparodha.dharmā" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: क्षुद्रकों के बहुसंख्यक होने से क्षुद्रकों के क्षय की पूर्ति की जा सकती है, मुख्यों के क्षय की नहीं।
english: The loss of lesser men can be made good, because lesser men are many; not the loss of chiefs.
lines_deva: शक्यः क्षुद्रक.क्षयः प्रतिसन्धातुं बाहुल्यात् क्षुद्रकाणाम्, न मुख्य.क्षयः
lines_iast: śakyaḥ kṣudraka.kṣayaḥ pratisandhātuṃ bāhulyāt kṣudrakāṇām, na mukhya.kṣayaḥ

words.gloss: because of superiority in spirit and intelligence

hindi: क्योंकि सत्त्व और प्रज्ञा की अधिकता के कारण, तथा क्षुद्रकों के उस पर आश्रित होने के कारण, हज़ारों में एक मुख्य होता है या एक भी नहीं होता।
english: For among thousands there is one chief, or not even one, because of his superiority in spirit and intelligence and because the lesser men depend on him.
lines_deva: सहस्रेषु हि मुख्यो भवत्य् एको न वा सत्त्व.प्रज्ञा.आधिक्यात् तद्.आश्रयत्वात् क्षुद्रकाणाम् इति
lines_iast: sahasreṣu hi mukhyo bhavaty eko na vā sattva.prajñā.ādhikyāt tad.āśrayatvāt kṣudrakāṇām iti

words.gloss: of one's own troops and the enemy's troops

hindi: "अपनी सेना और शत्रु की सेना में से अपनी सेना अत्यधिक दण्ड और कर से पीड़ित करती है और उसे रोका नहीं जा सकता; शत्रु की सेना से तो युद्ध किया जा सकता है, या पीछे हटकर अथवा सन्धि करके उससे छुटकारा पाया जा सकता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of one's own troops and the enemy's troops, one's own troops oppress with excessive fines and taxes and cannot be warded off; but the enemy's troops can be fought against, or got rid of by withdrawal or by a peace treaty,' say the teachers.

text_flags.why: 'praiyoddhum' is not a Sanskrit form; the infinitive of pra-√yudh is prayoddhum. Probable typing slip (stray 'i').

notes: cakra here = army, troops (sva-cakra: one's own; para-cakra: the enemy's). upasāra taken as 'moving away, withdrawal'; the sense 'approach, going over to the enemy' is also possible.
lines_deva: "स्व.चक्र.पर.चक्रयोः स्व.चक्रम् अतिमात्राभ्यां दण्ड.कराभ्यां पीडयत्य् अशक्यं च वारयितुम्, पर.चक्रं तु शक्यं प्रैयोद्धुम् उपसारेण सन्धिना वा मोक्षयितुम्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "sva.cakra.para.cakrayoḥ sva.cakram atimātrābhyāṃ daṇḍa.karābhyāṃ pīḍayaty aśakyaṃ ca vārayitum, para.cakraṃ tu śakyaṃ praiyoddhum upasāreṇa sandhinā vā mokṣayitum" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: by winning over or removing the chiefs among the men of the constituents
words.gram: m. inst. du. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

words.gloss: by plunder, slaughter, burning, destruction and carrying away

hindi: अपनी सेना का पीड़न प्रकृति-पुरुषों के मुख्यों को अनुकूल करके या हटाकर रोका जा सकता है, अथवा वह एक ही भाग को पीड़ित करता है; किन्तु शत्रु की सेना समस्त देश को पीड़ित करती हुई लूट, वध, दाह, विध्वंस और अपहरण से पीड़ित करती है।
english: Oppression by one's own troops can be warded off by winning over or removing the chiefs among the men of the constituents, or else it oppresses only one part; but the enemy's troops, oppressing the whole country, oppress by plunder, slaughter, burning, destruction and carrying away.
notes: prakṛti-puruṣa-mukhya: 'the chief men among the constituents' (the officers); vighāta taken as 'removal, suppression'.
lines_deva: स्व.चक्र.पीडनं प्रकृति.पुरुष.मुख्य.उपग्रह.विघाताभ्यां शक्यते वारयितुम् एक.देशं वा पीडयति, सर्व.देश.पीडनं तु पर.चक्रं विलोप.घात.दाह.विध्वंसन.अपवाहनैः पीडयति-इति
lines_iast: sva.cakra.pīḍanaṃ prakṛti.puruṣa.mukhya.upagraha.vighātābhyāṃ śakyate vārayitum eka.deśaṃ vā pīḍayati, sarva.deśa.pīḍanaṃ tu para.cakraṃ vilopa.ghāta.dāha.vidhvaṃsana.apavāhanaiḥ pīḍayati-iti

words.gloss: of a dispute among the constituents and a dispute with the king
bringing double rations, wages and exemptions

hindi: "प्रकृतियों के विवाद और राजा के साथ विवाद में से प्रकृतियों का विवाद प्रकृतियों में भेद डालने वाला है और शत्रुओं के आक्रमण लाता है, जबकि राजा के साथ विवाद प्रकृतियों को दुगुना भोजन-भत्ता, वेतन और कर-छूट दिलाने वाला होता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of a dispute among the constituents and a dispute with the king, a dispute among the constituents divides the constituents and brings on attacks by enemies, whereas a dispute with the king brings the constituents double rations, wages and exemptions,' say the teachers.

text_flags.why: 'prakṛiti' is a misspelling of prakṛti (stray 'i' after ṛ); the compound is written correctly elsewhere in the line.

notes: rāja-vivāda = a dispute of the constituents with the king (who must then win them back with double rations, wages and exemptions); 'a dispute between kings' is the alternative, less likely since war between kings is the para-cakra case of 13-15. bhakta = food rations.
lines_deva: "प्रकृति.राज.विवादयोः प्रकृइति.विवादः प्रकृतीनां भेदकः पर.अभियोगान् आवहति, राज.विवादस् तु प्रकृतीनां द्वि.गुण.भक्त.वेतन.परिहार.करो भवति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "prakṛti.rāja.vivādayoḥ prakṛiti.vivādaḥ prakṛtīnāṃ bhedakaḥ para.abhiyogān āvahati, rāja.vivādas tu prakṛtīnāṃ dvi.guṇa.bhakta.vetana.parihāra.karo bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: by winning over the chiefs of the constituents
by removing the ground of the quarrel

hindi: प्रकृतियों का विवाद प्रकृतियों के मुख्यों को अनुकूल करके या कलह के कारण को दूर करके रोका जा सकता है।
english: A dispute among the constituents can be warded off by winning over the chiefs of the constituents or by removing the ground of the quarrel.
lines_deva: शक्यः प्रकृति.विवादः प्रकृति.मुख्य.उपग्रहेण कलह.स्थान.अपनयनेन वा वारयितुम्
lines_iast: śakyaḥ prakṛti.vivādaḥ prakṛti.mukhya.upagraheṇa kalaha.sthāna.apanayanena vā vārayitum

words.gram: f. nom. pl. pres. mid. part. vi-√vad

hindi: और विवाद करती हुई प्रकृतियाँ परस्पर स्पर्धा के कारण उपकार करती हैं।
english: Moreover, constituents who are disputing render service through their mutual rivalry.
lines_deva: विवदमानास् तु प्रकृतयः परस्पर.सङ्घर्षेण-उपकुर्वन्ति
lines_iast: vivadamānās tu prakṛtayaḥ paraspara.saṅgharṣeṇa-upakurvanti

words.gloss: to be settled by double activity

hindi: किन्तु राजा के साथ विवाद प्रकृतियों के पीड़न और उच्छेद के लिए होता है और दुगुने व्यायाम से सिद्ध होता है।
english: But a dispute with the king leads to the oppression and extirpation of the constituents and is to be settled by double exertion.
notes: prakṛtīnām goes with pīḍana-ucchedanāya; whose double exertion settles the dispute (the king's, most likely) is not stated, so it is left open in both languages.
lines_deva: राज.विवादस् तु पीडन.उच्छेदनाय प्रकृतीनां द्वि.गुण.व्यायाम.साध्य इति
lines_iast: rāja.vivādas tu pīḍana.ucchedanāya prakṛtīnāṃ dvi.guṇa.vyāyāma.sādhya iti

words.gloss: of amusement by the country and amusement by the king
destruction of the fruits of works
benefit to artisans, craftsmen, performers, those living by speech, courtesans and traders
words.gram: m. acc. sg. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

hindi: "देश के विहार और राजा के विहार में से देश का विहार तीनों कालों में होने से कर्मों के फल का नाश करता है, जबकि राजा का विहार कारीगरों, शिल्पियों, नट-कुशीलवों, वाणी से जीविका चलाने वालों, रूपाजीवाओं और वैदेहक व्यापारियों का उपकार करता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of amusement by the country and amusement by the king, amusement by the country, taking place at all three seasons, causes destruction of the fruits of works; whereas amusement by the king benefits artisans, craftsmen, performers, those who live by speech, courtesans and traders,' say the teachers.
notes: vihāra = diversion, pleasure-pursuit; traikālya taken as 'at all three times (seasons)'. vāg-jīvana = those who live by speech (bards, reciters); rūpa-ājīvā = women living by their beauty, courtesans.
lines_deva: "देश.राज.विहारयोर् देश.विहारस् त्रैकाल्येन कर्म.फल.उपघातं करोति, राज.विहारस् तु कारु.शिल्पि.कुशीलव.वाग्.जीवन.रूप.आजीवा.वैदेहक.उपकारं करोति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "deśa.rāja.vihārayor deśa.vihāras traikālyena karma.phala.upaghātaṃ karoti, rāja.vihāras tu kāru.śilpi.kuśīlava.vāg.jīvana.rūpa.ājīvā.vaidehaka.upakāraṃ karoti" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: the toil of works (object of avadhā)
for the sake of laying aside (the toil)
by forcible seizures, demands for presents, and appropriation of goods, houses and labour

hindi: देश का विहार कर्मों के श्रम को दूर करने के लिए थोड़ा-सा खा लेता है और खाकर फिर कर्मों में लग जाता है; किन्तु राजा का विहार स्वयं और वल्लभों के द्वारा बलपूर्वक छीनने, उपहार की माँग तथा पण्य, घर और कार्य के हड़पने से पीड़ित करता है।
english: Amusement by the country consumes a little, in order to lay aside the toil of works, and having consumed it, turns again to application to works; whereas amusement by the king oppresses, both by himself and through his favourites, with forcible seizures, demands for presents, and appropriation of goods, houses and labour.
notes: avadhā = laying aside (ava-√dhā): karma-śramam avadhā-artham 'in order to lay aside the toil of work'; alpam is the object of bhakṣayati. svayaṃ-grāha = taking by one's own hand (forcible seizure); praṇaya = demand for a present; paṇya-agāra-kārya-upagraha = seizure of goods, houses and labour. Alternative segmentation: paṇya-agāra = shop, warehouse (paṇyāgāra, cf. 2.4), giving 'appropriation of shops and (their) business'. Segmentation of this long compound is uncertain.
lines_deva: देश.विहारः कर्म.श्रमम् अवधा.अर्थम् अल्पं भक्षयति भक्षयित्वा च भूयः कर्मसु योगं गच्छति, राज.विहारस् तु स्वयं वल्लभैश् च स्वयं.ग्राह.प्रणय.पण्य.अगार.कार्य.उपग्रहैः पीडयति-इति

words.gloss: of the favourite queen and the prince
by forcible seizures, demands for presents, and appropriation of goods, houses and labour

hindi: "सुभगा और कुमार में से कुमार स्वयं और वल्लभों के द्वारा बलपूर्वक छीनने, उपहार की माँग तथा पण्य, घर और कार्य के हड़पने से पीड़ित करता है, और सुभगा विलास के उपभोग से" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of the favourite queen and the prince, the prince oppresses, both by himself and through his favourites, with forcible seizures, demands for presents, and appropriation of goods, houses and labour; the favourite queen, by her enjoyment of luxuries,' say the teachers.
notes: subhagā = the king's favourite woman (favourite queen). Compound as in unit 23.
lines_deva: "सुभगा.कुमारयोः कुमारः स्वयं वल्लभैश् च स्वयं.ग्राह.प्रणय.पण्य.अगार.कार्य.उपग्रहैः पीडयति, सुभगा विलास.उपभोगेन" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "subhagā.kumārayoḥ kumāraḥ svayaṃ vallabhaiś ca svayaṃ.grāha.praṇaya.paṇya.agāra.kārya.upagrahaiḥ pīḍayati, subhagā vilāsa.upabhogena" ity ācāryāḥ

lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: by the minister and the chaplain
because of association with worthless people

hindi: कुमार को मन्त्री और पुरोहित के द्वारा रोका जा सकता है, किन्तु सुभगा को नहीं, मूर्खता और निरर्थक लोगों की संगति के कारण।
english: The prince can be restrained by the minister and the chaplain; not the favourite queen, because of foolishness and association with worthless people.
notes: samyogāt: the e-text writes m for the anusvāra before y (Devanagari सम्योग); saṃyogāt in the split. Not flagged as a typo.
lines_deva: शक्यः कुमारो मन्त्रि.पुरोहिताभ्यां वारयितुम्, न सुभगा बालिश्याद् अनर्थ्य.जन.सम्योगाच् च-इति
lines_iast: śakyaḥ kumāro mantri.purohitābhyāṃ vārayitum, na subhagā bāliśyād anarthya.jana.samyogāc ca-iti

words.gloss: of a guild and a chief

words.gram: m. inst. du. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

hindi: "श्रेणी और मुख्य में से श्रेणी अपनी बहुसंख्या के कारण नियन्त्रण में न आने वाली होकर चोरी और साहस से पीड़ित करती है, जबकि मुख्य कार्यों में अनुग्रह और विघात के द्वारा पीड़ित करता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of a guild and a chief, a guild, being uncontrollable because of its numbers, oppresses by theft and violence; a chief, by favouring and obstructing work,' say the teachers.
notes: śreṇī = a guild or corporation (of craftsmen or soldiers); sāhasa = violence, forcible action.
lines_deva: "श्रेणी.मुख्ययोः श्रेणी बाहुल्याद् अनवग्रहा स्तेय.साहसाभ्यां पीडयति, मुख्यः कार्य.अनुग्रह.विघाताभ्याम्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "śreṇī.mukhyayoḥ śreṇī bāhulyād anavagrahā steya.sāhasābhyāṃ pīḍayati, mukhyaḥ kārya.anugraha.vighātābhyām" ity ācāryāḥ

words.gloss: because of having the same character and vices
by winning over one section of the guild's chiefs

hindi: श्रेणी के सदस्यों का शील और व्यसन समान होने से, अथवा श्रेणी के मुख्यों के एक भाग को अनुकूल कर लेने से, श्रेणी को सरलता से फेरा जा सकता है।
english: A guild is easily turned round, because its members have the same character and the same vices, or by winning over one section of the guild's chiefs.
notes: vyasana in samāna-śīla-vyasanatvāt = the habits/vices of the guild members (not the Book 8 sense 'calamity of a constituent'), hence 'vices' / व्यसन.
lines_deva: सुव्यावर्त्या श्रेणी समान.शील.व्यसनत्वात्, श्रेणी.मुख्य.एक.देश.उपग्रहेण वा
lines_iast: suvyāvartyā śreṇī samāna.śīla.vyasanatvāt, śreṇī.mukhya.eka.deśa.upagraheṇa vā

words.gloss: by injuring the lives and property of others
words.gram: m. inst. du. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

hindi: स्तम्भ से युक्त मुख्य दूसरों के प्राण और द्रव्य का उपघात करके पीड़ित करता है।
english: A chief who is possessed of obstinacy oppresses by injuring the lives and property of others.
notes: stambha = stiffness, obstinacy, obstructiveness; the same word names the section 'stambha-varga' (unit 48), where it is rendered 'obstruction'.
lines_deva: स्तम्भ.युक्तो मुख्यः पर.प्राण.द्रव्य.उपघाताभ्यां पीडयति-इति
lines_iast: stambha.yukto mukhyaḥ para.prāṇa.dravya.upaghātābhyāṃ pīḍayati-iti

words.gloss: of the Treasurer and the Collector
by spoiling what has been done and by penalties
enjoying the fruit assigned to him

hindi: "सन्निधाता और समाहर्ता में से सन्निधाता किए हुए काम में दोष निकालकर और दण्ड लगाकर पीड़ित करता है, जबकि समाहर्ता कार्यालय के कर्मचारियों की देखरेख में रहकर निर्दिष्ट फल का उपभोग करने वाला होता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of the Treasurer and the Collector, the Treasurer oppresses by spoiling what has been done and by penalties; the Collector, being supervised by the office staff, enjoys the fruit assigned to him,' say the teachers.
notes: saṃnidhātṛ = treasurer (keeper of stores); samāhartṛ = collector-general. kṛta-vidūṣaṇa taken as 'faulting / spoiling work already done'; karaṇa = the office, its clerks. 'samnidhātṛ' in the e-text writes m for the anusvāra.
lines_deva: "सम्निधातृ.समाहर्त्रोः सम्निधाता कृत.विदूषण.अत्ययाभ्यां पीडयति, समाहर्ता करण.अधिष्ठितः प्रदिष्ट.फल.उपभोगी भवति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "samnidhātṛ.samāhartroḥ samnidhātā kṛta.vidūṣaṇa.atyayābhyāṃ pīḍayati, samāhartā karaṇa.adhiṣṭhitaḥ pradiṣṭa.phala.upabhogī bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ

in taking the property of others

hindi: सन्निधाता दूसरों के द्वारा व्यवस्थित किए हुए, कोश में डालने योग्य धन को ग्रहण करता है; किन्तु समाहर्ता पहले अपने लिए अर्थ बनाकर पीछे राजा का अर्थ बनाता है या उसे नष्ट कर देता है, और दूसरों का धन लेने में अपने ही निश्चय से चलता है।
english: The Treasurer receives what is to be put into the treasury after it has been settled by others; the Collector, however, first makes wealth for himself and afterwards makes the king's wealth or destroys it, and in taking the property of others he acts on his own authority.
lines_deva: सम्निधाता कृत.अवस्थम् अन्यैः कोश.प्रवेश्यं प्रतिगृह्णाति, समाहर्ता तु पूर्वम् अर्थम् आत्मनः कृत्वा पश्चाद् राज.अर्थं करोति प्रणाशयति वा, पर.स्व.आदाने च स्व.प्रत्ययश् चरति-इति

words.gloss: of the frontier officer and the traders
by letting thieves loose and by taking more than the dues
by favours of goods and goods in exchange
words.gram: m. inst. pl. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

hindi: "अन्तपाल और वैदेहक व्यापारियों में से अन्तपाल चोरों को छूट देकर और देय शुल्क से अधिक लेकर वणिक्-पथ को पीड़ित करता है, जबकि वैदेहक पण्य और प्रतिपण्य के अनुग्रह से उसे समृद्ध करते हैं" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of the frontier officer and the traders, the frontier officer harms the trade route by letting thieves loose and by taking more than the dues; the traders, on the other hand, make it prosper by favours of goods and goods in exchange,' say the teachers.

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. mid. part. √kṛ

hindi: अन्तपाल पण्यों के आगमन को अनुग्रह देकर जीविका चलाता है; किन्तु वैदेहक मिलकर पण्यों के भाव घटाते-बढ़ाते हुए एक पण पर सौ पण और एक कुम्भ पर सौ कुम्भ के हिसाब से जीविका चलाते हैं।
english: The frontier officer subsists by favouring the inflow of goods; the traders, however, combining together and raising and lowering the prices of goods, make their living at a hundred paṇas on a paṇa and a hundred kumbhas on a kumbha.

english: Land occupied by the well-born, or land occupied by cattle herds? 'Land occupied by the well-born, even though yielding great produce, is not fit to be freed, since it serves as a source of soldiers, for fear of harm in a calamity; land occupied by cattle herds, on the other hand, being fit for cultivation, is fit to be freed,

words.gloss: for fear of harm in a calamity
useful for the treasury and for draught animals
words.gram: f. nom. sg. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

words.gloss: in case of obstruction to the sowing of crops

hindi: कुलीनों के द्वारा अधिकृत भूमि अत्यन्त महान् उपकार करने वाली होने पर भी विपत्ति में बाधा के भय से छुड़ाने योग्य है; किन्तु पशुओं के झुण्डों के द्वारा अधिकृत भूमि कोश और वाहनों के लिए उपकारी होने से छुड़ाने योग्य नहीं है, सिवाय उस दशा के जब वह अन्न की बुवाई में बाधा डालती हो।
english: Land occupied by the well-born, even though of exceedingly great benefit, is fit to be freed, for fear of harm in a calamity; land occupied by cattle herds, on the other hand, being useful for the treasury and for draught animals, is not fit to be freed, except where it obstructs the sowing of crops.
notes: Kautilya turns the teachers' reason (vyasana-ābādha-bhayāt) round: the high-born occupants are themselves the danger in a calamity. vāhana = draught and riding animals.
lines_deva: अभिजात.उपरुद्धा भूमिर् अत्यन्त.महा.उपकारा-अपि क्षमा मोक्षयितुं व्यसन.आबाध.भयात्, पशु.व्रज.उपरुद्धा तु कोश.वाहन.उपकारिणी न क्षमा मोक्षयितुम्, अन्यत्र सस्य.वाप.उपरोधाद् इति
lines_iast: abhijāta.uparuddhā bhūmir atyanta.mahā.upakārā-api kṣamā mokṣayituṃ vyasana.ābādha.bhayāt, paśu.vraja.uparuddhā tu kośa.vāhana.upakāriṇī na kṣamā mokṣayitum, anyatra sasya.vāpa.uparodhād iti

hindi: "प्रतिरोधकों और आटविकों में से प्रतिरोधक रात में घात लगाकर चलते हैं, शरीर पर आक्रमण करते हैं, नित्य सक्रिय रहते हैं, सैकड़ों-हज़ारों का अपहरण करते हैं, प्रधान पुरुषों को कुपित करते हैं और छिपे रहते हैं; जबकि आटविक सीमान्त के वनों में विचरण करते हैं, प्रकट और दृश्य होकर चलते हैं, और एक ही प्रदेश को हानि पहुँचाते हैं" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Of robbers and forest chiefs, robbers move in ambush by night, attack persons, are constant, carry off hundreds and thousands, provoke the principal men, and remain concealed; forest chiefs, on the other hand, move in the frontier forests, go about openly and in plain sight, and harm only one region,' say the teachers.

text_flags.why: 'ahapārin' is not a word; apahārin 'carrying off' fits (cf. 'pahartāraḥ in unit 43). Transposed letters.
dṛśya 'visible' needs ś, not s; 's' for 'ś' is a typing slip.
possible: pratyanta 'frontier' is the expected word (cf. pratyanta elsewhere in the book); 'pratyantara' looks like a slip. Kept as doubtful.

notes: sattra here = ambush, hiding place. vyavahitāḥ taken as 'concealed, screened off' (contrasted with prakāśāḥ dṛśyāḥ of the forest tribes). pradhāna-kopakāḥ: 'causing the principal men to be angry', i.e. troubling the leading people. pratirodhaka = robber, highwayman (one who waylays).
lines_deva: "प्रतिरोधक.आटविकयोः प्रतिरोधका रात्रि.सत्त्र.चराः शरीर.आक्रमिणो नित्याः शत.सहस्र.अहपारिणः प्रधान.कोपकाश् च व्यवहिताः प्रत्यन्तर.अरण्य.चराश् च-आटविकाः प्रकाशा दृस्याश् चरन्ति, एक.देश.घातकाश् च" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "pratirodhaka.āṭavikayoḥ pratirodhakā rātri.sattra.carāḥ śarīra.ākramiṇo nityāḥ śata.sahasra.ahapāriṇaḥ pradhāna.kopakāś ca vyavahitāḥ pratyantara.araṇya.carāś ca-āṭavikāḥ prakāśā dṛsyāś caranti, eka.deśa.ghātakāś ca" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: of the same nature as kings

hindi: प्रतिरोधक असावधान का हरण करते हैं; वे थोड़े, मन्द, और सरलता से जाने और पकड़े जा सकने वाले होते हैं; किन्तु आटविक अपने ही प्रदेश में स्थित, बहुसंख्यक और पराक्रमी होते हैं, प्रकट रूप से युद्ध करने वाले, देशों के अपहरणकर्ता और हन्ता, तथा राजा के समान धर्म वाले होते हैं।
english: Robbers rob the careless; they are few, dull, and easy to find out and to catch; forest chiefs, on the other hand, are settled in their own territory, numerous and valiant, fighting openly, plunderers and slayers of countries, and of the same nature as kings.

text_flags.why: 'aparahanti' is not a form; apaharanti 'they rob' (apa-√hṛ) is required by the genitive pramattasya and the parallel apahartāraḥ. Transposed letters.
possible: 'fighting' from √yudh is yodhin; 'yodin' (d for dh) looks like a slip.

notes: kuṇṭha = blunt, feeble. deśānām construed with apahartāraḥ and hantāraḥ.
lines_deva: प्रतिरोधकाः प्रमत्तस्य-अपरहन्ति, अल्पाः कुण्ठाः सुखा ज्ञातुं ग्रहीतुं च, स्व.देशस्थाः प्रभूता विक्रान्ताश् च-आटविकाः प्रकाश.योदिनो ऽपहर्तारो हन्तारश् च देशानां राज.सधर्माण इति
lines_iast: pratirodhakāḥ pramattasya-aparahanti, alpāḥ kuṇṭhāḥ sukhā jñātuṃ grahītuṃ ca, sva.deśasthāḥ prabhūtā vikrāntāś ca-āṭavikāḥ prakāśa.yodino 'pahartāro hantāraś ca deśānāṃ rāja.sadharmāṇa iti

words.gloss: of a deer forest and an elephant forest

hindi: मृगवन और हस्तिवन में से मृग बहुसंख्यक होते हैं, बहुत माँस और चर्म देने वाले, थोड़े चारे के कारण कम कष्ट देने वाले, और सरलता से नियन्त्रित होने वाले होते हैं;
english: Of a deer forest and an elephant forest: deer are numerous, supply much meat and hide, cause little trouble over fodder, and are easy to control;
notes: 'vanayoḥ mṛgāḥ' is left unsandhied in the e-text (print vanayor mṛgāḥ); not flagged. manda-grāsa-avakleśin: 'causing little distress by (their) eating', i.e. costing little to feed. No teachers/Kautilya opposition in units 44-47; the sentence continues in unit 45.
lines_deva: मृग.हस्ति.वनयोः मृगाः प्रभूताः प्रभूत.मांस.चर्म.उपकारिणो मन्द.ग्रास.अवक्लेशिनः सुनियम्याश् च
lines_iast: mṛga.hasti.vanayoḥ mṛgāḥ prabhūtāḥ prabhūta.māṃsa.carma.upakāriṇo manda.grāsa.avakleśinaḥ suniyamyāś ca

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. pass. part. √grah

words.gloss: for the ruin of the country

hindi: हाथी इसके विपरीत होते हैं, और पकड़े जाते समय तथा दुष्ट होने पर देश के विनाश का कारण बनते हैं।
english: Elephants are the opposite, and while being captured, or when vicious, they lead to the ruin of the country.
lines_deva: विपरीता हस्तिनो गृह्यमाणा दुष्टाश् च देश.विनाशाय-इति
lines_iast: viparītā hastino gṛhyamāṇā duṣṭāś ca deśa.vināśāya-iti

words.gloss: of benefit from one's own sthānīya and from the enemy's
providing grain, cattle, gold and raw materials

hindi: अपने स्थानीय नगर और शत्रु के स्थानीय नगर के उपकार में से अपने स्थानीय नगर का उपकार धान्य, पशु, हिरण्य और कुप्य देने वाला तथा आपत्ति में जनपदवासियों के जीवन को धारण करने वाला होता है;
english: Of benefit from one's own sthānīya (provincial town) and from that of the enemy, benefit from one's own sthānīya provides grain, cattle, gold and raw materials and sustains the life of the country people in adversity;
notes: sthānīya = a fortified provincial town (the head of a group of villages); upakāra = benefit, help rendered. kupya = raw materials (forest produce, base metals), per glossary. Sentence continues in unit 47.
lines_deva: स्व.पर.स्थानीय.उपकारयोः स्व.स्थानीय.उपकारो धान्य.पशु.हिरण्य.कुप्य.उपकारो जानपदानाम् आपद्य् आत्म.धारणः
lines_iast: sva.para.sthānīya.upakārayoḥ sva.sthānīya.upakāro dhānya.paśu.hiraṇya.kupya.upakāro jānapadānām āpady ātma.dhāraṇaḥ

hindi: शत्रु के स्थानीय नगर का उपकार इसके विपरीत होता है।
english: benefit from the enemy's sthānīya is the opposite.
lines_deva: विपरीतः पर.स्थानीय.उपकारः
lines_iast: viparītaḥ para.sthānīya.upakāraḥ

words.gloss: obstruction by an ally or forest tribes
words.gram: m. nom. sg. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

hindi: ये पीड़न हैं। आभ्यन्तर स्तम्भ मुख्यों का स्तम्भ है, बाह्य स्तम्भ मित्र और आटवी का स्तम्भ है। ४८। यह स्तम्भ-वर्ग है।
english: These are the afflictions. Internal obstruction is obstruction by chiefs; external is obstruction by an ally or forest tribes. 48. This is the group of obstructions.

text_flags.why: final 'h' for visarga 'ḥ' (Devanagari वर्गह् with halanta h); the word is vargaḥ.

notes: GROUPING: the e-text puts the number '| 48 |' inside this line, before 'iti stambha-vargaḥ'; the closing phrase belongs with the same unit (end of the stambha section), and the 'iti pīḍanāni' at the start closes the list of afflictions (units 1-47). stambha = obstruction (stiffening, blocking) by the persons named.
lines_deva: इति पीडनानि - आभ्यन्तरो मुख्य.स्तम्भो बाह्यो मित्र.अटवी.स्तम्भः । ४८ । इति स्तम्भ.वर्गह्
lines_iast: iti pīḍanāni - ābhyantaro mukhya.stambho bāhyo mitra.aṭavī.stambhaḥ | 48 | iti stambha.vargah

words.gloss: carried off by a neighbouring king or forest tribes
words.gram: m. nom. sg. (tat-puruṣa over a dvandva)

words.gloss: the group of impediments to the treasury

hindi: उन दोनों से और यथोक्त पीड़नों से पीड़ित, मुख्यों के पास अटका हुआ, परिहारों से क्षीण, बिखरा हुआ, गलत ढंग से संगृहीत, सामन्त या आटवी के द्वारा हरण किया हुआ — यह कोश-सङ्ग-वर्ग है।
english: Afflicted by those two and by the afflictions as stated, held up with the chiefs, impaired by exemptions, scattered, wrongly collected, carried off by a neighbouring king or forest tribes: this is the group of impediments to the treasury.
notes: The masculine adjectives describe the treasury (kośa), the implied subject; tābhyām = the two obstructions (internal and external) of unit 48. saṅga = sticking, impediment. sāmanta = neighbouring king.
lines_deva: ताभ्यां पीडनैर् यथा.उक्तैश् च पीडितः, सक्तो मुख्येषु, परिहार.उपहतः, प्रकीर्णो, मिथ्या.संहृतः, सामन्त.अटवी.हृत इति कोश.सङ्ग.वर्गः
lines_iast: tābhyāṃ pīḍanair yathā.uktaiś ca pīḍitaḥ, sakto mukhyeṣu, parihāra.upahataḥ, prakīrṇo, mithyā.saṃhṛtaḥ, sāmanta.aṭavī.hṛta iti kośa.saṅga.vargaḥ

words.gloss: for the sake of the growth of the country

hindi: देश की वृद्धि के लिए पीड़नों के उत्पन्न न होने में, उत्पन्न हुए पीड़नों के निवारण में, तथा स्तम्भ और सङ्ग के नाश में प्रयत्न करना चाहिए।
english: For the sake of the growth of the country, one should strive for the non-arising of afflictions and for warding off those that have arisen, and for the destruction of obstructions and impediments.
notes: Closing śloka; the subject (the king) is unexpressed in the Sanskrit.
lines_deva: पीडनानाम् अनुत्पत्ताव् उत्पन्नानां च वारणे
यतेत देश.वृद्ध्य्.अर्थं नाशे च स्तम्भ.सङ्गयोः
lines_iast: pīḍanānām anutpattāv utpannānāṃ ca vāraṇe
yateta deśa.vṛddhy.arthaṃ nāśe ca stambha.saṅgayoḥ
